theme: Pre-market range break-and-go — does RTH take out the pre-market H/L?

definitions.PMH: Pre-market high (highest price in 4:00-9:30 ET window)
definitions.PML: Pre-market low (lowest price in same window)
definitions.PM_color: Green if 9:30 RTH open > 4:00 PM-open; red if below
definitions.PMH_broken: Any RTH bar's high exceeded PMH
definitions.PML_broken: Any RTH bar's low went below PML
definitions.Sweep: Both PMH AND PML broken during RTH
definitions.Contained: Neither broken — RTH stays inside PM range

aggregate_break_rates.key_finding: Only 1 day in 229 (0.44%) stayed inside the PM range. RTH ALMOST ALWAYS takes out at least one side of pre-market.

conditional_on_pm_color.key_finding: Strong directional mirror. After a green PM session, 84% chance the PMH gets broken (vs 57% the PML). After red PM, 83% PML break vs 55% PMH. PM session direction is a strong predictor of which side of the PM range RTH will break.

first_break_direction_unconditional.key_finding: Without color conditioning, first-break direction is a coin flip. The directional edge from PM color (above) shows up in EOD outcomes, not first-break timing.

small_pm_lt_100pts.interpretation: Tight pre-market compresses, likely to break both sides during RTH

medium_pm_100_300pts.interpretation: Most common bucket. About 1 in 3 sweep both sides.

large_pm_gt_300pts.interpretation: Wide pre-market range — RTH usually only takes one side. Small sample though.

by_pm_range_size.key_finding: Sweep rate inversely correlated with PM range size. Tight PM ranges sweep both sides more often (53%) than wide PM ranges (19%). Compression begets sweeps.

range_stats.interpretation: PM range averages 154 NQ points, RTH averages 308 — exactly 2x. PM accounts for ~54% of the day's total range on average.

key_findings.1: Pre-market levels are nearly always traded. Only 0.44% of days (1 in 229) stayed inside the PM range.
key_findings.2: PMH break by EOD: 71%, PML break by EOD: 69%, both broken: 40%. Each side has individual ~70% break probability.
key_findings.3: PM color is a clean directional predictor: green PM -> 84% PMH break, red PM -> 83% PML break. Mirror pattern.
key_findings.4: First-break direction without conditioning is a coin flip (49/48). Color is what separates the winners from losers.
key_findings.5: Small PM ranges (<100 pts) sweep both sides 53% of the time. Large PM ranges (>300 pts) only 19% — suggesting wide PM = directional move that holds.
key_findings.6: PM range averages ~54% of RTH range. The premarket session contributes meaningful price discovery.

sample_size_caveat: 229 days = ~11 months. Aggregate stats trustworthy to ±3pp. Sub-buckets like 'large PM range' (n=16) are anecdotal — wider CIs.
